notes: Upper Market / Castro / Eureka Valley (15th to below 19th St, Corona Heights edge to east of Noe), sheet 7 of the 1960 map: Market St cuts the grid on a diagonal, leaving triangular and trapezoid blocks; Beaver and Flint run at angles round Corona Heights; narrow alleys (Pond, Prosper, Dehon, Harlow). What the map shows here: thin lines (3-4 px) close each block; zoning borders are heavy lines (6-9 px). Some run down street middles (down Flint St, x about 1946-1952 between its two thin lines; along the street at x 2058-2066 north of 16th; along Hartford, x 2239-2245; along Noe north of 18th; across 17th and 18th), others cut through blocks (the N-S line at x 2056-2072 through the blocks west of Castro; the stairs through the block Beaver/16th/Castro and through both Market triangles; the R-2 box over Pond/Prosper; the R-3 box east of Noe; the C-2 stairs in the blocks east of Castro; y about 2262 in the block west of Market; y about 2525 and 2605 in the left column; y about 2818-2825 in the bottom row). Told apart by weight and by continuity (a block line closes at the block's corners; a zoning border runs on across streets and blocks). How corners were set: from the scan's dark pixels. Paper (pixels lighter than 134) was split into connected pieces; the pieces belonging to each block were chosen by eye on ruled close-ups and a map of the pieces; each block's pieces were united, grown over ink only by up to 4 px (to the outer edge of the block's own thin line, also bridging zoning borders through the block), holes filled, smoothed 3x3 and simplified at 1.5 px. Hand edits: where letters or zoning-box lines cut into an outline, four outlines were typed by hand from the measured corners (triangle 2367-2555 x 1916-2082 under the C of C-2; middle block 2444-2501 x 2137-2329 under R-2; the two blocks either side of the alley east of Noe, 2609-2819 x 2345-2543) and the top-left of block 2132-2304 x 2142-2291 under R-4 was filled with a hand rectangle. Judgment calls: (1) Corona Heights (x 1900-1980, y 1905-2215) is hill land with no thin line of its own on its inner sides; only zoning borders separate it from the lots along Beaver (1930-1980 x 1957-2030), along the curve of 16th (1908-1975 x 2112-2163) and the block south of that curve (1923-2106 x 2135-2211). No street divides them, so all are ONE block, with the dead-end curve of 16th (y 2163-2175, ending at x about 1912) cutting into it. The owner may prefer Corona land as open and the lots as their own blocks. (2) Flint St (diagonal, x about 1936-1959 at y 2030) is two thin lines with a heavy zoning border down its middle; the narrow paper either side of the border is street. Beaver St's diagonal leg (x about 1940-1990) is a narrow street too. The labels BEAVER, FLINT, POND and PROSPER are printed inside blocks. (3) The narrow E-W strip y 2212-2229, x 1900-2065 (two thin lines, ending at the zoning border beside Market) is read as a street. (4) Pond and Prosper are alleys of 5-7 px paper between three narrow blocks (x 2371-2438, 2444-2501, 2507-2579). (5) East of Noe between 17th and 18th a narrow sloped strip (y 2424-2451) between two blocks is read as an alley (street), with the R-3 box drawn over it. (6) A thin line at x 2141-2143 runs on along Castro's east side across the mouth of 18th St (y 2554-2575); read as not a block edge, and 18th St east of Castro is left as street. (7) Dehon and Harlow are dead-end alleys notched into block 2603-2815 x 2130-2325. Blocks at the box's sides and bottom row (y 2780-2845) are cut by the box.
drawn_by: Claude (AI), 2026-11-23: blocks chosen by eye on ruled close-ups and a map of the scan's paper pieces; corners measured from the scan's dark pixels (each block's paper grown over ink by up to 4 px to the outer edge of its own line, simplified at 1.5 px); four outlines typed by hand from those measurements where letters cut the line; checked on the labels picture
